description: Reader-facing aerial creature and ecology entries.

entries.title: Sheffels
entries.summary: Large, placid herd animals drift through the skies and provide food, hide, transport, and livelihood to sky communities.
body: Sheffels are buoyant herd beasts adapted to open air and floating-island pasture. Their calm temperament permits domestication and aerial herding, while their bodies supply meat, milk, leather, and other necessities.
Herd movement spreads seeds and nutrients between islands, making Sheffels economically important and ecologically disruptive when overgrazed.

sections.heading: Legacy Stat Block
body: The source includes fifth-edition statistics, traits, and actions requiring conversion.

entries.title: Skyflayer
entries.summary: A feared aerial predator uses speed, concealment, and sudden attacks to hunt travelers and flying animals.
body: Skyflayers are legendary ambush hunters of the open air. They exploit clouds and poor visibility, striking isolated prey before withdrawing into the sky.
Their reputation makes sightings significant to pilots, herders, and settlements whose livestock graze beyond defended airspace.

sections.heading: Legacy Stat Block
body: The source includes fifth-edition statistics and combat actions requiring conversion.

entries.title: Skywhales
entries.summary: Skywhales grow from agile young animals into immense elders that shape migration, culture, and aerial ecosystems.
body: Young, adult, and elder Skywhales occupy different ecological scales. Their movement through the skies influences smaller creatures, currents, and the communities that track or protect them.
They carry cultural and spiritual importance, but hunting, habitat pressure, and conflict with air traffic threaten their survival.

sections.heading: Legacy Age Stat Blocks
body: The source gives separate fifth-edition statistics for young, adult, and elder Skywhales. Conversion is required.

entries.title: Sky Maws
entries.summary: Parasitic aerial predators attach to creatures, ships, and magical objects to drain vitality and power.
body: Sky Maws wait within clouds, latch onto vulnerable hulls or living prey, and siphon energy over time. They are usually solitary but gather into devastating seasonal swarms able to exhaust fleets or islands.
Known variants include the elusive Cloud Maw, storm-feeding Tempest Maw, and immense Abyss Maw. Some cultures treat them as agents of ecological balance despite their danger.

sections.heading: Legacy Size Stat Blocks
body: The source gives small, normal, and huge fifth-edition Sky Maw statistics and combat abilities requiring conversion.

entries.title: Flufftrounce
entries.summary: A harmless winged rabbit-like creature disperses seeds and is valued as a companion and source of delicate fur.
body: Flufftrounces travel in small herds between islands, feeding on airborne plants, fruit, insects, and spores. Their buoyant wings and nervous bursts of speed make them difficult to catch.
Their fur leaves a drifting cloud, and their movements distribute plant life across isolated habitats.

sections.heading: Legacy Stat Block
body: The source includes fifth-edition statistics and evasive abilities requiring conversion.

entries.title: Common Aerial Hunters
entries.summary: Aetherhawks, Storm Eagles, Sky Vultures, and Skywyrms occupy distinct predatory and scavenging niches.
body: Aetherhawks manipulate wind and dive at speed. Storm Eagles channel weather and electricity. Sky Vultures track blood and decay across great distances. Skywyrms are small serpentine dragons with lightning breath and unusual stealth.
Together they form a recognizable group of hazards, hunting animals, omens, and potential trained companions throughout the inhabited skies.

sections.heading: Legacy Stat Blocks
body: The source supplies fifth-edition statistics for all four creatures. Conversion is required.
